author: Sergio Mendoza
description: Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz said he’ll reshuffle his cabinet to bring it “closer” to the population, as food, fuel and medicine run low in major cities amid a blockade by protesters.
title: Bolivia to Overhaul Cabinet as Highway Blockades Strangle La Paz

description: Today, Bloomberg's Mike McKee reports from the Federal Reserve as the committee releases the minutes of its last meeting, where officials warned the central bank could need to raise rates if inflation continued to run persistently above the 2% target. Then, Bloomberg Technology host Ed Ludlow breaks down new reporting on a potential IPO for artificial intelligence giant OpenAI. Plus, Bloomberg's Myles Miller on US charges against Cuba's Raul Castro ratcheting up tensions between the two countries. Then, Bloomberg's Alex Semenova and Thomas Thornton discuss his bearish stance and what risks are most pressing to the market. Finally, Bloomberg's Norah Mulinda and Scion Group CEO Rob Bronstein on Scion's deal with Ares Management to buy $910M in student housing properties. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Officials Warned of Rate-Hike if Inflation Persists | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 5/20/2026

author: Biz Carson
description: Google co-founder Sergey Brin is continuing to push deeper into California politics by donating to a group that opposes a proposed tax hike on businesses with highly-paid executives in San Francisco.

On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss Tuesday's primary elections. On today's show, Joe and Kailey are live from Georgia Tech in Atlanta.  (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Iran warned it would retaliate beyond the Middle East if the US or Israel attacks it again, following renewed threats from President Donald Trump. description: Andrew Young, former US UN ambassador and civil rights activist, joined Balance of Power to discuss the election results in Georgia and the current political climate. Young said whether it's the midterms this year or the 2028 election, voters are going to deliver a judgment on the current direction of the country. (Source: Bloomberg)

description: President Trump and the candidates he endorsed in the congressional primary had a good night on Tuesday. But, as Tyler Kendall asks, will it be enough to keep control of the House and Senate come November? (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche made the announcement Wednesday in Miami. The charges stem from the downing of two civilian aircraft in 1996. They were operated by a Florida-based exile group called Brothers to the Rescue. Bloomberg's Myles Miller reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Charges Former Cuban Leader Raúl Castro With Murder

description: Amazon.com Inc. founder Jeff Bezos expressed support for New York’s plan to impose a new tax on luxury second homes in the city, noting that higher levies on out-of-towners is a reasonable way to raise revenue.

description: President Donald Trump says he's in "no hurry" to reach a deal with Iran to end the war. Trump says it seems like Iran does not have the "good of the people" in mind. He spoke to reporters on Wednesday.  (Source: Bloomberg)

description:
The US and Iran seem deadlocked over how to turn their fragile ceasefire into a more permanent peace, with neither side toning down its belligerent rhetoric in recent days.
Monica Guerra, Morgan Stanley Wealth Management Executive Director and Head of US Policy, discusses her takeaways from US primaries this week, Trump foreign policy, and what to expect from ongoing peace negotiations in the Middle East. (Source: Bloomberg)

description: The Republican-led US Senate signaled rising opposition to continuing the Iran war in a procedural vote Tuesday. Louisiana Senator Bill Cassidy, whose re-election bid President Donald Trump thwarted in a Republican primary Saturday, joined three other GOP senators voting to clear the hurdle and move toward a final vote on a resolution to cease hostilities. description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, the Chinese President Xi Jinping warned against resuming military operations in the Middle East, at the start of talks with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin. Xi stepped up calls for a truce, saying "a comprehensive ceasefire is imperative". US President Trump has threatened to resume strikes on Iran in the coming days if there's no deal to end the war.

Talks between Samsung and its largest labor union have broken down, with workers planning to go on strike on Thursday. A walkout at the world's largest memory chipmaker risks disrupting the global technology supply chain. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: China's Xi Hosts Putin, Steps Up Call for Iran Ceasefire | Daybreak Europe 05/20/2026

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" is live from Georgia Tech in Atlanta, Georgia focusing on the Midterm Primaries. On today's show, Andre Dickens, Mayor of Atlanta, says turnout has been “pretty good” on primary day in Georgia and that affordability is top of mind for voters. Adam Stulberg, Chair and Professor at Georgia Tech’s Sam Nunn School of International Affairs, says energy markets are unlikely to return to their pre-conflict normal, as displaced tankers, depleted supply stocks, damaged infrastructure and weakened market shock absorbers keep pressure on prices. Josh McKoon, Chairman of the Georgia Republican Party, discusses President Trump’s influence in Republican primaries, the race he expects will head to a runoff, the consideration of new congressional maps and why Georgia remains a very competitive state.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Polls Open on 'Mini' Super Tuesday | Balance of Power: Late Edition 05/19/2026
